property_summary: For any call to Put, the unlockTime stored for msg.sender must equal the maximum of the provided _unlockTime and block.timestamp; the buggy version leaves it as the default 0, violating this rule.

After a successful Put, calling Collect with a non-zero amount and MinSum condition satisfied should succeed when block.timestamp > unlockTime; the bug makes unlockTime 0, so block.timestamp > 0 always holds, making Collect always succeed when balance >= MinSum, whereas the reference requires block.timestamp > the passed _unlockTime which may be in the future.

After a Put by an actor, calling Collect with a non-zero amount when the actor's balance is at least MinSum and the amount should revert if block.timestamp <= the unlockTime set during Put; the bug sets unlockTime=0, causing the call to succeed instead of revert.

After any sequence of Put calls, the unlockTime stored in the contract should never be less than the block.timestamp at the time of the last Put; the mutant allows an unlockTime in the past, enabling premature Collect.
After any Put, the stored unlockTime is always >= the block.timestamp at the time of that Put; the mutant allows a smaller _unlockTime, breaking this invariant.

After a Put call, the Acc[actor].unlockTime should be at least block.timestamp if _unlockTime is not greater; the mutant sets unlockTime to a potentially smaller past value, allowing immediate Collect.

After a successful Collect, the contract's balance must decrease by the collected amount; the mutant allows a Put with a past unlockTime followed by a Collect that reverts due to MinSum logic, leaving the balance unchanged but still observable.

After any Put, the contract's ETH balance (address(c).balance) must equal the sum of all Acc balances; the bug allows a reentrant caller to exploit the unprotected modifier and drain ETH, breaking this invariant.

After any sequence of Put calls, the Acc balance of each caller must equal the total ETH they deposited minus any successful Collect withdrawals; the bug allows a reentrant caller to reuse the same msg.value to inflate their balance on the same Put call, breaking the equality.

After a Put call, a reentrant attacker can call Collect within its fallback to withdraw funds while the original Put has already added to the balance but not yet locked, making the contract's ETH balance drop below the sum of all Acc balances for some input.

After any successful Put call, the caller's Acc balance increase equals msg.value, but a reentrant attacker can cause the increase to be applied multiple times with a single call, making the balance increase greater than the sent msg.value.

After a reentrant call from an adversarial contract in Put, the reentrant call can call Put again and inflate its own Acc balance without sending additional Ether; thus after the top-level Put completes, the sum of all Acc balances will be strictly greater than the contract's Ether balance for some inputs.

After any single Put call, the contract's state must reflect exactly one execution of the Put function; the buggy version allows reentrancy that causes the effects of Put to be applied more than once, breaking the token balance invariant.

After any Put call, the sum of the caller's Acc.balance increase must equal msg.value; reentrancy in the buggy version allows Put to be re-entered which can cause more than msg.value to be recorded into the caller's balance, breaking the invariant that delta balance == msg.value.

After Put, the contract's ETH balance equals the sum of all Acc balances, but the bug lets a reentrant callee repeat Put within the same call, inflating its Acc balance beyond the actual ETH received, breaking the equality.

After a single call to Put(msg.value > 0), the caller's Acc.balance must equal exactly msg.value because the reference uses a reentrancy lock; the buggy version lacks the lock so an adversarial callee can reenter Put during its receive() and inflate the caller's balance beyond msg.value.

After the callee of Collect with a non-zero amount causes a reentrant Put from its fallback, the caller's Acc.balance must decrease by exactly the amount collected; the buggy version fails to set the reentrancy lock, allowing the reentrant Put to increase the balance before the subtraction, resulting in a higher final balance.

After a successful Put call, any subsequent call to Put must succeed (not revert) in the reference contract, but the buggy contract's modifier never resets locked_, causing the next call to incorrectly revert.

After a successful Put call, any subsequent external call must be able to execute without permanent lockout; the buggy modifier never clears locked_, permanently blocking re-entry, which violates the invariant that the lock state should eventually be reset.
After a successful Put, a subsequent Put from a different address must succeed; the buggy modifier never clears locked_, so any later call reverts.

After a successful Put call, a subsequent Collect call that meets all withdrawal criteria (sufficient balance, amount, and time) must eventually succeed (allow the call and decrease balance), but the buggy modifier never clears locked_, causing the Collect call to revert and leave the balance unchanged.
If a Collect succeeds, the timestamp must be strictly after the caller's unlockTime stored in the contract.
Collect must revert when block.timestamp is not strictly greater than the caller's unlockTime and the balance conditions are met.
